title: Browser Access: clientless ZPA access to web applications
aliases: browser access vs zcc vs pra

prose.text: Browser Access is ZPA's clientless path for web applications. A question about it usually falls into one of the areas below, and each is answered in its own subject.

steps.label: Is Browser Access the right path?
steps.text: What it carries, what the browser and server must support, and how sessions and reauthentication work: [[zpa.browser-access.requirements]]. RDP, SSH and VNC go to [[zpa.pra]].

steps.label: Why does the user see a certificate error?
steps.text: External versus internal hostname: [[zpa.browser-access.hostnames]], with the untrusted-certificate setting in [[zpa.browser-access.backend-options]].

steps.label: Which certificate covers which name?
steps.text: Wildcards, managed and custom certificates and the CNAME: [[zpa.browser-access.certificates]].

steps.label: What can the hosting segment not use?
steps.text: Double Encryption, ports and CNAME resolution, whether Multimatch applies (an earlier version of the article said so; the current one does not), and the per-application keys: [[zpa.browser-access.segment-constraints]].

steps.label: How do access rules treat browser sessions?
steps.text: Client type and the criteria that do not apply: [[zpa.browser-access.policy]].

steps.label: How do tools write the segment?
steps.text: [[zpa.browser-access.tooling]], with Ansible child handling in [[zpa.app-segments.ansible-children]]. Terraform lifecycle defects are in [[zpa.terraform.app-segment-lifecycle]].
